pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:736 The blocking verdict is computed against waivers read from the range's own commit messages, which the authoring agent writes itself. The ruleset requires no human approval, so the gated party can still open its own gate for any non-secret rule by naming that rule.

techniques.evidence: scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:736 The waiver comes from text the gated party writes, and .github/rulesets/main.json has no required-review rule, so nothing independent of the author drives pending→open. The 2026-09-05 change narrowed what a waiver covers but did not change who may issue one.
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:132 A grant now matches only its (rule, file, optional line) tuple. A shapeless or unmatched trailer is reported and never widens to the whole range.
scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:670 Each waived finding is rendered with the stated reason, and the trailer persists in git log next to the commit's author.

scripts/review/agent-review.mjs:222 Any severity the model returns other than exactly 'blocking' (e.g. 'Blocking', 'high', missing) falls through to the mildest bucket, 'note', with no marker. renderMarkdown (lines 226-227) does the same, so a malformed severity is waved through quietly.

scripts/review/agent-review.mjs:271 When no reviewer can be asked, the lens exits 0 (and line 255 also returns 0 when there is no comparable base). The required 'Agent review (judgement)' check therefore passes on an unjudged change. The loud stdout is honest, but the verdict is allow, not deny. Contrast constitution-check, which returns 2 for a check that did not run.

scripts/review/agent-review.mjs:89 A blocking verdict must name the specific rule or ADR it breaks. That rule comes from a rubric assembled from the repo's own written rules (rubric.mjs), so there is a named thing to compare against.

pairs.registryProposal: fail-closed-profile-for-headless is written for agent tool approval. It does not say whether an automated review lens that cannot run may resolve to allow when a sibling deterministic gate has already run. kp argues that it may. The technique should state explicitly whether 'another gate covered it' is an acceptable fallback or still counts as unknown-treated-as-safe.

pairs.subject: hitl-approval
pairs.evidence: app/features/hiring/decisions/decisionsAiReviewCardLogic.ts:25 An approval payload (screening, queued-reject, scorecard or offer) that will not parse collapses to the same null as 'no detail at all', with no marker. The decision card for an adverse-action gate then renders with no body and no signal that its payload was unreadable.

techniques.evidence: app/features/hiring/decisions/decisionsAiReviewCardLogic.ts:25 No parse-failure flag is returned, and the consumer CandidateDecisionBar renders `isOffer && parsed ?` and `parsed?.recommendation` silently. An unreadable payload is not raised to a loud state and not marked.

app/features/hiring/decisions/decisionsScreenWaveMachine.ts:32 The commit echoes a signed preview token and spare list. If the set differs, the server refuses with 'mismatch' and the reducer forces a fresh preview, so approval binds to the exact set shown.

app/features/hiring/decisions/decisionsScreenWaveMachine.ts:33 Staleness is checked at commit time: a token already spent means the wave already landed. The modal reloads the queue instead of re-running or mis-narrating.

app/features/hiring/decisions/decisionsScreenWaveMachine.ts:34 A commit that names no approver is blocked for the life of the modal. The decider's identity is required, and its absence is never treated as fixable by re-previewing.

app/features/hiring/decisions/decisionsScreenWaveMachine.ts:150 Changing the target (a new exclusion) re-closes the approval and forces a fresh token. The committed view is frozen (line 145), and a new event type without a transition is a type error.
app/features/hiring/decisions/decisionsQueueTypes.ts:55 One predicate drives the header count, the role-filter counts and the empty state, so the badge cannot disagree with the rendered cards.
